sections.html:
Algonquin is a Fox River suburb about 40 miles northwest of the Chicago Loop, and a sale there can involve two counties because the village straddles the McHenry and Kane line. Roughly 78 percent of the village area is in McHenry County and the rest is in Kane County, so the county printed on your tax bill decides who records the deed and who collects the tax.

The population was 29,700 in 2020 and is estimated at 30,824 for July 1, 2025. Most of the housing is relatively young, since the count climbed from 5,684 in 1980 to 11,663 in 1990 and 23,276 in 2000. Owners occupy 88.2% of homes and value them at a typical $351,000. Gross rent runs a typical $1,723.

Location inside the village matters because Algonquin has distinct districts with different traffic and housing. Old Town sits along Main Street (Illinois Route 31) near the original village hall at 2 South Main Street, and exterior changes to any building in its historic district need a Certificate of Appropriateness from the village.

The Randall Road corridor on the western side is the retail spine. The manufacturing belt runs along Algonquin Road between Pyott Road and Route 31, west of Old Town. A buyer comparing a house near the industrial belt with one near the river will weigh noise and truck traffic differently, so an honest description saves time later.

Two school districts split the village, and the boundary often decides which houses draw the most interest from families. Community Unit School District 300 covers the area generally along and east of Randall Road. Consolidated School District 158, headquartered in Algonquin, serves the far western side. Confirm the assignment for your street before you put a school name in a listing.

sections.h2: Do I need a village permit before repairing or selling?
sections.html:
Algonquin requires a building permit before anyone erects, enlarges, alters, repairs, moves, improves, removes, converts or demolishes a building or structure. Small cosmetic jobs are exceptions. The Community Development Department says permit review can take up to five weeks, so repairs you want done before listing should start early.

Permit status for common jobs, Village of Algonquin permit information
ProjectPermit required?
Roof repair of 200 sq ft or lessNo
Siding repair of 200 sq ft or lessNo
Fence repair of 3 sections or lessNo
Patio sitting wall under 24 inchesNo
Gutters and downspoutsYes
Garage service doorYes
Radon mitigationYes, if electrical is needed for the fan

Anyone moving into a newly built home needs a certificate of occupancy before move-in. The village uses the 2018 International Residential Code and the 2018 International Property Maintenance Code, among others. Questions go to Community Development at (847) 658-2700, option 3, or permits@algonquin.org. If a prior owner finished a basement or deck, ask that office whether the permit was closed before you list.

Out-of-town buyers check the road network first. Randall Road is the multi-lane north and south arterial and runs six lanes between Harnish Drive and Corporate Parkway. Route 31 is the two-lane Main Street through downtown, and its intersection with Algonquin Road backs up at peak times. Illinois Route 25 runs along the eastern edge, and Pace Route 550 follows Randall Road between Crystal Lake and Elgin.

Fire and rescue come from one of three districts depending on the address: the Algonquin-Lake in the Hills Fire Protection District, the Huntley Fire Protection District or the Carpentersville Countryside Fire Protection District. Your tax bill names the districts that serve the parcel.

sections.h2: Property tax bills in McHenry County
sections.html:
McHenry County mails one bill and collects two installments. For the 2026 collection year, bills went out in early May and the installments were due June 9 and September 9. The payment office at 2100 N. Seminary Ave. in Woodstock takes payment at the window or drive-thru lanes from 7:30 to 5 on weekdays.

  • eCheck payments online carry no fee. Credit cards, debit cards and digital wallets add a 2.4% convenience fee.
  • Two 24-hour drop boxes, one walk-up and one drive-up, take checks and money orders payable to the McHenry County Collector. No cash.
  • Write the parcel number (PIN) on any check, and ask the Post Office for a postmark when mailing close to a due date.
  • The VIP Taxpayer program sends email and text reminders and lets owners switch to e-billing.

Parcels in the Kane County part of the village are billed by Kane County, so check the county name on the bill before you pay. At closing, ask the title officer to settle the current year's tax and any open installment between buyer and seller.

The County Recorder rejects documents that miss formatting or content rules, and a rejection can push back the date a buyer gets title. The Recorder wants a white 20-pound page with a half-inch clean margin on every side and a clear 3 by 5 inch box at the top right.

  • A deed needs the grantor's signature, the grantee's address and the full McHenry County legal description.
  • A Plat Act affidavit goes with the deed when the legal description is metes and bounds.
  • Either a completed exemption paragraph or the Illinois transfer declaration (PTAX-203 or MyDec) must accompany every deed. A MyDec filing must state "Closing Completed."
  • Every document needs "Prepared By" and "Mail To" lines with names and addresses.

Section 31-10 of the Property Tax Code sets the state transfer tax at 50 cents on each $500 block of value in the declaration. Ask the McHenry or Kane County Recorder, whichever holds your parcel, about any county stamp and the Rental Housing Support Program surcharge.

Owners here usually weigh three paths: an agent listing, a private sale and a sale to a buyer who takes the house as it stands. A listing fits a house ready for move-in. Selling privately skips the agent but leaves the permit, deed and declaration work to the owner and the closing attorney. A sale as-is fits a vacant, inherited or tenant-occupied property that needs work.

Whichever route you pick, an open permit or a missing certificate of occupancy will still come up at closing. A call to Community Development early in the process keeps the schedule intact. Then confirm your county from the parcel number, get the current-year tax settled with the title officer, and have the deed prepared to the Recorder's format rules before the signing date.

faqs.q: Which county handles my Algonquin deed and tax bill?
faqs.a: It depends on the parcel. About 78 percent of the village is in McHenry County and the rest is in Kane County. The county name on your tax bill tells you whom to ask.

faqs.q: Does Algonquin require a permit for a small roof repair?
faqs.a: Not for a repair of 200 square feet or less. Larger roof work, gutters and downspouts, and a garage service door do need permits.

faqs.q: When were McHenry County property tax installments due in 2026?
faqs.a: June 9 and September 9, 2026. Check the Treasurer's Office for the dates on the next bill, and pay online by eCheck to avoid the 2.4% fee charged on cards.

faqs.q: Does Algonquin Old Town have extra rules for exterior work?
faqs.a: Yes. A Certificate of Appropriateness is required for all exterior changes, additions and demolitions to buildings inside the historic district.

faqs.q: What must a MyDec filing say for McHenry County recording?
faqs.a: It must state "Closing Completed." The Recorder also needs the grantee's address, the legal description and a Plat Act affidavit if the description is metes and bounds.
